title: Second Serving — From Equipment Fault to Branch Recovery
notes: Actual moving user footage, edited chronologically. No fabricated application screens or outcomes.
This is a fictional operational scenario: a rice-cooker failure at DEMO Akasaka Pickup, with nine veggie bowls supplied by DEMO Shinjuku East.
The source shows an 18-minute estimate, zero transfer cost, a 10-minute approved route and a fresh 60-minute customer deadline.
Original audio is removed. Chrome password popups/account metadata and the right-hand recorder toolbar are excluded.
Waiting, repeated receipts, a validation stumble and unrelated branch browsing are shortened or omitted. Every accelerated segment is labelled.
The AI call/loading/response and the request-through-receipt confirmations remain at original playback speed.
Stock values are illustrative demo inputs, not measured business impact or safety validation.
outcome_note: The recorded UI shows a new route making Shinjuku eligible, then Requested → Approved → Preparing → On the way → Received for nine DEMO Veggie Rice Bowl servings. This is a simulated workflow in the prototype, not proof of a physical food delivery.
claims_note: No source-stock balance change, equipment repair or incident resolution is shown in this take. Captions explain the confirmation semantics but do not invent a stock delta, repair, measured savings or real customer adoption.

clips.label: ONE WORKSPACE FOR THE CHAIN
clips.caption: Branch operations and incident recovery for fast-food and takeaway chains.

clips.label: LOCAL MENUS, LOCAL READINESS
clips.caption: Switch branches to see what each store can sell with its own stock and equipment.

clips.label: BRANCH-OWNED INVENTORY
clips.caption: Akasaka tracks its own ingredients and stock balances.

clips.label: RECEIVE STOCK IN THE RIGHT UNIT
clips.caption: Record a stock receipt in the ingredient's measurement unit.

clips.label: A REASON AND AN AUDIT TRAIL
clips.caption: Save the receipt with a reason. The balance and movement history update.

clips.label: LINK SHARED INGREDIENTS
clips.caption: Choose which shared ingredients this branch tracks. Linking alone does not add stock.

clips.label: QUANTITIES, RESERVATIONS AND HISTORY
clips.caption: Branch inventory keeps quantities, reservations and recorded movements together.

clips.label: ONE SHARED INGREDIENT CATALOG
clips.caption: Ingredient definitions are shared across the chain. Stock quantities stay local.

clips.label: BRANCH EQUIPMENT OWNERSHIP
clips.caption: Akasaka's rice cooker is a branch-owned asset. Report a problem directly from its card.

clips.label: RECORD THE FAULT AND THE NEED
clips.caption: Confirm the cooker fault: nine veggie bowls need support within 60 minutes.

clips.label: CHECK RECOVERY CONSTRAINTS
clips.caption: No source is eligible yet. Support needs an approved route to the receiving branch.

clips.label: NVIDIA NEMOTRON ON NEBIUS
clips.caption: Request AI advice for manager review. No operational changes happen automatically.

clips.label: APPROVE THE DIRECTED ROUTE
clips.caption: Approve the demo route from Shinjuku East to Akasaka: 10 minutes of travel.

clips.label: A CHECKED SUPPORT OPTION
clips.caption: Eligible: 9 bowls · 18 minutes · ¥0

clips.label: REVIEW AND SEND THE REQUEST
clips.caption: Review source, destination and quantity. Sending does not reserve stock.

clips.label: APPROVE AND RESERVE
clips.caption: The source approves the request and reserves ingredients.

clips.label: PREPARE AND CONSUME STOCK
clips.caption: Starting preparation consumes ingredients at the source branch.

clips.label: RECORD DISPATCH
clips.caption: Confirm dispatch of the prepared dishes in this demo.

clips.label: CONFIRM DESTINATION RECEIPT
clips.caption: The receiving branch confirms the prepared meals have arrived in this demo.

clips.label: RECOVERY RECORDED, RESPONSIBILITY CLEAR
clips.caption: Nine bowls marked Received. Equipment repair and incident resolution remain separate.
